sessions.title: ACT AS: You are a Principal AI Engineer, Enterprise Data Architect, Data Quality Architect, and Gemini Enterprise solution architect with 20+ years of experience designing enterprise AI platforms. PROJECT: Migration Validator CURRENT ARCHITECTURE: The existing application validates migrations from: - PostgreSQL → Snowflake - Microsoft SQL Server → Snowflake - AWS Athena → Snowflake The existing system already contains: - Connection management - Schema extraction - Table discovery - Column discovery - Deterministic column matching - Fuzzy matching - Confidence scoring - AI resolution for ambiguous columns - CanonicalValidationPlan / plan.json - Type normalization rules - SQL generation - YAML validation configuration - Validation execution - Count validation - Data validation - Exclusions - Batch validation - Learning / feedback - Existing UI with: - Connections - Generate — Single Table - Generate — Batch - Rule Book - Exclusions - Usage & Cost IMPORTANT: DO NOT rebuild the Migration Validator. DO NOT replace existing functionality. DO NOT create a second parallel architecture. Inspect the repository first and extend the existing architecture. HACKATHON CONTEXT: We are participating in Stream 3 — Connectors for Gemini Applications. The highest-weight criterion is: Enabling Client Use Cases — 35% The goal is to demonstrate that the connector becomes a critical foundation for high-value enterprise AI use cases with measurable business value. PRIMARY OBJECTIVE: Turn Migration Validator into a Gemini-powered Migration Intelligence Connector. Gemini Enterprise should be able to interact with Migration Validator using secure, purpose-built tools and perform useful migration-validation workflows. DESIGN PRINCIPLE: Gemini should be the conversational intelligence layer. Migration Validator should remain the governed execution and data-validation layer. The architecture should become: Gemini Enterprise ↓ Migration Intelligence Connector ↓ Migration Validator APIs / tools ↓ PostgreSQL / MSSQL / Athena ↓ Snowflake ↓ Validation Engine ↓ Results ↓ Gemini explanation IMPLEMENT THE FOLLOWING CLIENT USE CASES: USE CASE 1 — Validate a Migration User asks Gemini: "Validate the customer migration from PostgreSQL to Snowflake." Gemini should: 1. Identify source and target. 2. Discover schema. 3. Identify source and target tables. 4. Build table/column mappings. 5. Apply deterministic mappings. 6. Escalate ambiguous mappings. 7. Resolve applicable rules. 8. Build or retrieve the canonical validation plan. 9. Generate validation SQL. 10. Execute validation. 11. Return a concise business-oriented result. Example response: Migration validation completed. Table: customer Source: PostgreSQL Target: Snowflake Schema: PASS Row Count: PASS Column Coverage: 100% Data Validation: 99.97% Warnings: - created_at required timestamp normalization - 1 target-only audit column excluded 3 columns require human review. USE CASE 2 — Investigate a Failed Migration User asks: "Why did the customer migration fail?" Gemini should retrieve validation results and explain: - failed validation - affected table - affected column - mismatch count - rule used - likely reason - recommended action Example: customer_id: 127 source records were not found in Snowflake. created_at: 0.8% timestamp mismatch. Likely cause: Timezone normalization mismatch. Recommended action: Review TIMESTAMP_UTC rule. USE CASE 3 — Migration Health / Portfolio Summary User asks: "Show me all migrations that need attention." Gemini should retrieve a compact summary: Total tables: 500 Passed: 440 Warnings: 45 Failed: 15 Human review: 20 Then identify: - low coverage - failed validations - ambiguous mappings - missing tables - target-only columns - rule failures USE CASE 4 — Ambiguous Mapping Review User asks: "Show me the column mappings that need my approval." Return: Table Source Column Target Column Confidence AI Recommendation Rule Reason Status Example: active_flag → IS_ACTIVE Confidence: 84% Recommended Rule: BOOLEAN_TO_NUMBER Status: HUMAN_REVIEW The user must be able to approve, modify, reject, or exclude the mapping through the UI. USE CASE 5 — Explain a Rule User asks: "Why did you normalize active_flag?" Gemini should retrieve the applicable Rule Book entry and explain: - source datatype - target datatype - semantic type - normalization - SQL transformation - validation strategy - rule status - rule scope USE CASE 6 — Coverage Analysis User asks: "Which tables have validation coverage below 95%?" Return a structured list with: - table - source coverage - target coverage - exclusions - reason - recommendation USE CASE 7 — Compare Migration Runs User asks: "Did the migration improve after the last run?" Compare historical validation results: - previous run - current run - failed tables - mismatch count - coverage - newly introduced issues - resolved issues USE CASE 8 — Human Approval Workflow Gemini should be able to initiate governed actions such as: approve_mapping reject_mapping modify_mapping approve_rule reject_rule approve_exclusion remove_exclusion approve_validation_plan Every write action must: - identify the authenticated user - record timestamp - record previous state - record new state - record reason - create audit history RULE: AI must NOT silently approve migration decisions. AI recommends. Human approves high-risk decisions. CanonicalValidationPlan stores the approved state. AI should NOT invent validation semantics when an approved Rule Book rule exists. BUILD A COMPACT TOOLSET: Prefer purpose-built tools such as: discover_connections list_databases list_schemas list_tables get_table_schema get_table_mapping get_column_mappings get_pending_reviews get_rule get_applicable_rules get_validation_plan generate_validation_plan generate_validation_sql execute_validation get_validation_result get_validation_failures get_migration_summary approve_mapping reject_mapping approve_rule approve_plan Do NOT expose huge database schemas or raw datasets to Gemini. Return compact structured responses optimized for token efficiency. IMPORTANT: Every tool must have: - clear description - strict input schema - strict output schema - error handling - authorization check - audit logging where applicable AI RESPONSE DESIGN: Gemini should summarize results instead of dumping raw SQL or thousands of rows. Provide: - status - key metrics - failures - warnings - recommendations - links/IDs to deeper details HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP UI: Extend the existing UI rather than creating a separate application. Add a Migration Review experience containing: 1. Table Mapping 2. Column Mapping 3. Confidence 4. AI Recommendation 5. Rule Used 6. Exclusions 7. Validation Strategy 8. Generated SQL Preview 9. Approval History 10. Approve / Reject / Modify controls CONFIDENCE POLICY: Use the existing confidence architecture as the starting point: >= 0.95: Auto accepted 0.75–0.95: AI-assisted / Human Review < 0.75: Unmatched / Mandatory Review Make thresholds configurable. MEASURABLE BUSINESS VALUE: Instrument the system to measure: - tables processed - columns processed - mappings automated - mappings requiring human review - validations automated - manual SQL avoided - validation execution time - human review time - failures detected - coverage - AI token usage Produce metrics that can be used in the hackathon presentation. SUCCESS CRITERIA: A judge should be able to interact with Gemini and perform at least these workflows: 1. "Validate this migration." 2. "Why did it fail?" 3. "Show me tables needing attention." 4. "Show me mappings requiring approval." 5. "Explain this rule." 6. "Approve this mapping." 7. "Show me the final validation status." The final experience must demonstrate that Gemini is not merely a chatbot over a database. Gemini must act as an intelligent interface to a governed migration-validation platform. IMPLEMENTATION REQUIREMENTS: Before modifying anything: 1. Inspect repository structure. 2. Identify existing connectors, orchestrator, plan, rule registry, SQL generator, execution engine, UI and configuration. 3. Reuse existing interfaces wherever possible. 4. Avoid duplicate logic. 5. Maintain backward compatibility. 6. Add tests. 7. Add logging. 8. Add configuration through environment/config files. 9. Do not expose secrets. 10. Provide a clear implementation summary and files changed. FINAL DELIVERABLE: Provide: - architecture changes - tool definitions - API/interface definitions - Gemini integration flow - UI changes - human approval workflow - audit model - test cases - demo scenario - measurable ROI metrics - setup instructions
